environment.browser: Chrome (Playwright channel=chrome) HeadlessChrome/153.0.0.0, persistent profile, fresh per run
environment.audio_encoder: Opus (no AAC encoder in this Chromium)

real_components: Chrome process quit and relaunched on the same on-disk profile
expected: After a full browser restart the project reopens with the same plan, the same pinned voice takes (no re-synthesis), a restorable render cache, and exports a valid MP4; an edit after reopen partially re-renders from the restored cache.
comparison_semantics: Pinned inputs compared by SHA-256 recomputed from restored bytes. Re-encoded video compared on pre-encode frame hashes + ffprobe structure (encoder is not run-to-run reproducible here, ENC-01); reused scenes compared on decoded frames (ffmpeg framemd5), which must be bit-identical because their encoded chunks come from the restored cache.
claim_supported: A complete cartoon project (plan, 6 pinned Kokoro takes, render cache) saved in Chrome survives quitting and relaunching the browser: it reopens with identical take bytes and zero TTS calls, re-exports a valid MP4 with identical pre-encode frames and identical narration, and a post-reopen scene-2 edit reuses the restored intro/outro chunks bit-exactly.
claim_not_supported: save/reopen through the editor UI (store is called from the harness page; UI wiring is pending)
background-image / audio-asset persistence in a real browser (covered by contract tests only; the sample plan uses procedural backgrounds)
storage eviction by the browser under real quota pressure
multi-tab concurrent editing beyond CAS conflict
